title: Inventory opens on the Active tab, with the Inactive tab beside it
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-TABS-01) is active and tracked at {Location-A}.
custom_steps:
1. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
  2. Look at the area between the page title "Inventory" and the table.
  3. Type {Part-A} in the Search box.
  4. Click the Inactive tab.
  5. Click the Active tab.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: The Inventory page opens with two tabs, "Active" and "Inactive", and "Active" is already the selected tab (shown in blue) without you clicking it.
  • Step 2: The two tabs sit on their own line directly under the title "Inventory". The search and filter row (Search, Bin Location, Category, Supply, the columns icon, the ⋮ menu and New Inventory Part) sits below the tabs, not beside them.
  • Step 3: The Active tab lists {Part-A} (1 row).
  • Step 4: "Inactive" becomes the selected tab and {Part-A} is not listed there.
  • Step 5: "Active" is selected again and {Part-A} is listed again.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10814 (Story 1, Active and Inactive Tabs on the Inventory List); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S1-R1, S1-R2, S1-R3, S1-R4, S1-R8, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 3.5 (The Inactive tab), board 4.0 (Before: the Inventory list today), board 4.1 (The actions menu), 13 Oct copy.   • S1-R8: “The Active and Inactive tabs sit on their own line under the page title, above the search and filter row.”
  • S1-R3: “The Active tab lists only parts that are active at the current location.”

title: Parts that existed before the release are active and tracked
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
  • Inventory parts {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-RELEASE-01, -02 and -03) existed at {Location-A} before the Part Lifecycle build was deployed, and nobody has changed them since.
  • Part {Part-B} has a quantity above 0 and a saved Min and Max (for example Min 1 and Max 6).
  • You can pick a second location, {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310), in the location selector.
custom_steps:
1. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
  2. Type {Part-A} in the Search box.
  3. Replace the search text with {Part-B}.
  4. Replace the search text with {Part-C}.
  5. Click the Inactive tab.
  6. Type {Part-A} in the Search box, replacing any text there.
  7. Replace the search text with {Part-B}.
  8. Replace the search text with {Part-C}.
  9. Click the Active tab.
  10. Type {Part-B} in the Search box, replacing any text there.
  11. Click the {Part-B} row.
  12. Click Cancel.
  13. Open Settings and look through its menu, including the Parts group and Roles & Permissions, for an on or off setting for the Active and Inactive tabs or for tracking.
  14. Pick {Location-B} in the location selector.
  15. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 2 to 4: Each of {Part-A}, {Part-B} and {Part-C} is listed on the Active tab, and its Total Qty column shows a number, never "Not Tracked".
  • Steps 6 to 8: None of the three is listed on the Inactive tab.
  • Step 11: Edit Inventory Part opens with a green "Active" pill in the title row, Part Status set to Active, and the "Track quantities and cost of goods" switch on, with Min and Max showing the values {Part-B} had before the deployment (for example 1 and 6).
  • Step 13: There is no setting that turns the Active and Inactive tabs or tracking on or off: the feature is simply on.
  • Step 15: {Location-B} also shows the Active and Inactive tabs.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10814 (Story 1, Active and Inactive Tabs on the Inventory List); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S1-R5, S1-R5a, S1-R5b, S13-R3, S4-R8, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 3.1 (Part Status in the dialog), board 5.3 (The list says Not Tracked), 13 Oct copy. Tech plan "Parts Lifecycle Update — Technical Implementation Plan" (7 Oct 2026), §4 Database Changes (Data migrations). Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R5: “Every part that exists on the day of release is active.”
  • S1-R5a: “Every part that exists on the day of release is tracked.”
  • S1-R5b: “The feature is on for every shop on the day of release. There is no rollout setting.”
  • PRD Story 1 context note (S1-R5): “S1-R5 describes the data on release day, not a rule the system keeps enforcing. Nothing makes a part active again on its own.”
  • S13-R3: “When editing, the title row shows the part's saved status as a pill beside the close X: "Active" in green, or "Inactive" in grey.”
  • S4-R8: “An untracked part shows "Not Tracked" in the Inventory list's Total Qty column instead of a quantity.”
  • Tech plan §4 Database Changes (Data migrations): “Release-day state comes from `DEFAULT 1` (active and tracked, S1-R5/R5a). There is no separate backfill and no rollout setting (S1-R5b).”

title: Each tab lists only the parts with that status at the current location
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin who can pick two locations in the location selector, {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) and {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LOCTAB-01) is active at {Location-A} and is not stocked at {Location-B}.
  • Inventory part {Part-B} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LOCTAB-02) is stocked at both locations with the same part number: inactive at {Location-A} and active at {Location-B}.
  • Both part numbers start with the same text, {Prefix-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-LOCTAB).
custom_steps:
1. Pick {Location-A} in the location selector in the top bar.
  2. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
  3. Type {Prefix-A} in the Search box.
  4. Click the Inactive tab.
  5. Pick {Location-B} in the location selector.
  6. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
  7. Type {Prefix-A} in the Search box, replacing any text there.
  8. Click the Inactive tab.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: At {Location-A} the Active tab lists {Part-A} and does not list {Part-B}: 1 row.
  • Step 4: At {Location-A} the Inactive tab lists {Part-B} and does not list {Part-A}: 1 row.
  • Step 7: At {Location-B} the Active tab lists {Part-B}, because it is still active there: 1 row. {Part-A} is not listed, because it is not stocked at {Location-B}.
  • Step 8: At {Location-B} the Inactive tab lists no part starting with {Prefix-A}. Making {Part-B} inactive at {Location-A} did not change it at {Location-B}.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10814 (Story 1, Active and Inactive Tabs on the Inventory List); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S1-R3, S1-R4, §2 Feature Overview, §4 Key Decisions, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas board 3.5 (The Inactive tab), board 2.5 (Lethbridge: renamed there too), 13 Oct copy. Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S1-R3: “The Active tab lists only parts that are active at the current location.”
  • S1-R4: “The Inactive tab lists only parts that are inactive at the current location.”
  • PRD §2 Feature Overview (Core functionality): “Both states belong to the part at one location. The same part at another location keeps its own states.”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions (Active and tracked are set per location): “Active and tracked are set per location. A part is stocked at a location, and whether the shop still sells it, or counts it, is that location's call. Changing either state at one location never changes the same part at another location.”

Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919); the Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View', 'Part Library & Inventory → Create & Edit' and 'Part Library & Inventory → Delete' and can see costs and prices.
  • Parts → Inventory is open on the Active tab at {Location-A}.
  • Bin {Bin-A} is the default bin of {Location-A} (for example General Storage), the bin New Inventory Part fills in.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-CORETRK-01, described {Description-A}, for example ZZAUTOTEST PL CORE TRACKING) is active and tracked at {Location-A}, with 2 in {Bin-A} and a Core Charge of $25.00, so it has a core.
  • The core of {Part-A} is described "Core for {Description-A}"; it is {Core-A}.
  • The new global search (Search in the top bar) is on, as it is by default for every account.
custom_steps:
1. Search the part number of {Part-A} in Inventory and click its row.
  2. Click the Track quantities and cost of goods switch so it is off.
  3. Click Save.
  4. Click Search in the top bar and type Core for {Description-A}.
  5. Read the {Core-A} result.
  6. Press Esc, then click the {Part-A} row again.
  7. Click the switch so it is on.
  8. Click Save.
  9. Search Core for {Description-A} in the top bar again and read the {Core-A} result.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: {Part-A} reads "Not Tracked" in Total Qty, and its Core column still reads $25.00.
  • Steps 4 and 9: If global search lists no "Core for {Description-A}" result, the core's tracking cannot be seen on any screen: this part cannot be checked by hand; write "not checked by hand" in the result comment.
  • Step 5: The {Core-A} result shows "Not Tracked" in place of its available badge: it changed with the same save as {Part-A}, and you did not edit the core.
  • Step 9: The {Core-A} result shows an available badge again (a number, not "Not Tracked"), changed by the same save that turned {Part-A} back on.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10818 (Story 5, Change Tracking on an Existing Part); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S5-R9, S9-R20 (how global search shows an untracked part) and §4 Key Decisions (A core follows its part), read 13 Oct 2026. Design: no board shows a core. Where cores show: QA lead's answer of 9 Oct 2026, situation 5. Source-verified 13 October 2026; not yet build-verified (no Part Lifecycle QA build exists).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R9: “The part's core is tracked or untracked together with the part, in the same save. A core added to the part later, or in the same save, takes the part's tracking state.”
  • PRD §4 Key Decisions: “A core follows its part. A core is never activated, deactivated, tracked or untracked on its own.”
  • S9-R20: “Global search shows "Not Tracked" for an untracked part, in place of its "{n} available" badge.”

title: The parts import never saves a tracked part without a bin
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete' and opens Settings → Data Import.
  • No part numbered {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-NOBIN-01) exists at {Location-A}.
  • Import file {Import-file-A} has one row for {Part-A} with the grid_location cell (the import's name for Bin Location) left empty.
custom_steps:
1. Open Settings → Data Import → Inventory.
  2. Upload {Import-file-A}.
  3. Run the import.
  4. Read the message the import shows for the {Part-A} row.
  5. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
  6. Type {Part-A} in the Search box.
  7. Click the {Part-A} row, if the list shows one.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 4 and 6: Either the row is refused with "At least one bin must be provided." and no {Part-A} is listed, or the row is imported and {Part-A} is listed as a tracked part.
  • Step 7: If {Part-A} was imported, Edit Inventory Part shows "Track quantities and cost of goods" on and at least one bin location marked "Default". A tracked {Part-A} saved with no bin location at all fails the case.
  • Steps 1 to 7: The other refusals of this rule cannot be produced from the screens: a tracked part sent with bins but none marked as the default ("At least one bin must be marked as default.") and a request to turn tracking on for a part with no bin ("At least one bin must be provided."). Write "not checked by hand" for them in the result comment.

title: A rename through the public API carries over like a rename in the part dialog
custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Admin who can pick two locations in the location selector, {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919) and {Location-B} (for example Staging Lethbridge - 4310). The Admin role has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete'.
  • Inventory part {Part-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-PUBAPI-01) is active at both {Location-A} and {Location-B}, on one Part Library entry.
  • Purchase order {Purchase-order-A} (for example PO-1001) at {Location-A} has an open line for {Part-A}, not yet received.
  • A connected system has changed {Part-A}'s number to {Number-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-PUBAPINEW-02) through ShopView's public API. This cannot be done in the ShopView screens.
custom_steps:
1. Pick {Location-A} in the location selector in the top bar.
  2. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
  3. Type {Number-A} in the Search box.
  4. Click the clock icon (tooltip "Part History") at the left of the {Number-A} row.
  5. Pick {Location-B} in the location selector.
  6. In the top bar click Parts, then click Inventory in the left menu.
  7. Type {Number-A} in the Search box.
  8. Click the clock icon at the left of the {Number-A} row.
  9. Pick {Location-A} in the location selector.
  10. In the top bar click Parts, then click Purchase Orders in the left menu.
  11. Open {Purchase-order-A}.
  12. In the top bar click Parts, then click Part Library in the left menu.
  13. Type {Part-A} in the Search box.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 3: At {Location-A} the part is listed as {Number-A}.
  • Step 4: Part History at {Location-A} has the entry "Part number updated | Original number: {Part-A} | New number: {Number-A} | Changed through: Public API", with no "Changed at".
  • Step 8: Part History at {Location-B} has the same entry, also ending "| Changed through: Public API".
  • Step 11: The open line of {Purchase-order-A} reads {Number-A}.
  • Step 13: No Part Library entry is found for {Part-A}: the part was renamed in place and no entry was made for the old number.
  • Steps 1 to 13: This case needs a change made through the public API. If no connected system made it, write "public API change not available, not checked by hand" in the result comment and mark the case Blocked.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog); story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change); PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, as edited 9 Oct 2026 (Ready for dev), S13-R19d, S13-R18, S13-R19, S10-R23, S10-R25a, read 13 Oct 2026; design canvas: no board shows this behaviour (13 Oct copy).   • S13-R18: “Saving a changed number renames the part in place. The part keeps its identity, its history, and every line that holds it. Its Part Library entry is renamed with it, and its core takes the same number. No new Part Library entry is created.”

custom_steps:

  12. Click the {Part-A} row.

custom_expected:
